conviction_note: Findings sum to +1.4. They net a known drop in license revenue ($3.75M in Q2 against $0.8M documented for Q3) against July script momentum, a capital-allocation decision management tied to Q3 data, and a crowded short (29% of shares, 11.8 days to cover) that is covering into a stock priced at about half its estimated cash. The scaled number is 0: p_up 50 with abs_move 12. The name has sold 6 of its last 8 prints, three of them by 18-23%, and that reaction history offsets the cash-floor and squeeze setup. The gap between the +1.4 sum and 0 is that disagreement, not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue $4.20M, EPS -$0.97, from one source only: MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LENZ/earnings/ (read 2026-10-28). The company gives no guidance. There is no second agreeing estimate source, so every finding that depends on the bar is capped small. The line the stock actually trades on (VIZZ monthly packs and product revenue; Q2 was ~27,000 packs and $1.74M) has no sourced consensus. My estimate: Q3 product revenue ~$2.0-2.6M plus the $0.8M Arrotex license recognised in July gives total ~$2.8-3.4M, about 25% under the $4.2M headline bar.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest via equibles.com (https://equibles.com/stocks/lenz/shortinterest, read 2026-10-28): 9,095,817 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 11.81 days to cover. That is down from 10,560,869 on 2026-09-30 and 11.86M on 2026-07-15, so shorts are covering into the print. It is ~29% of the 31.42M shares outstanding; MarketBeat puts it at 31.57% of float. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so no skew. Put/call OI is 0.53 on only 275 contracts total, which carries no information. Holders: FMR cut its stake from ~11.8% (Feb 2026) to 5.7% (1,783,202 shares) as of 2026-08-31 (13G/A filed 2026-09-08). BlackRock Portfolio Management filed a new 5.2% 13G (event date 2026-09-30, filed 2026-10-27). Millennium is at 3.7% (13G/A filed 2026-10-21). No Form 4 insider filings since July.

findings.finding: License revenue falls in Q3, so headline revenue and EPS likely miss MarketBeat's single-source bar. The 10-Q's subsequent-events note documents only $0.8M of Arrotex license revenue recognised in July 2026, against $3.75M in Q2 (a $2.5M Théa milestone plus $1.25M Everest sublicense). With product revenue of ~$2.0-2.6M, total Q3 revenue comes to ~$2.8-3.4M against $4.20M consensus. With SG&A at or above Q2's $39.4M (117 territories deployed by end-Q2, national TV live from July 6), the net loss per share likely lands around -$1.05 to -$1.20 against a -$0.97 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (reported 2026-03-24) missed revenue ($1.59M vs $3.09M) and EPS (-$1.16 vs -$0.91); stock -17.9%. Q1 2026 missed EPS (-$1.32 vs -$1.10); -20.8%. Q2 2026 headline revenue beat ($5.49M vs $2.38M, mostly license); only -3.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The MarketBeat $4.2M figure only makes sense if it carries license revenue resembling Q2's. If the market had priced a ~$3M total, the published consensus would sit near $3M. The bar has one source, and buy-side models probably already strip license timing, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001815776/000181577626000051/a991q226pressrelease.htm) itemises Q2 license revenue as $2.5M Théa plus $1.25M Everest, both one-time events. It is the same company, so this is not independent; it is the comparison base.

findings.finding: Script momentum entering Q3. On the Q2 call (2026-08-11), management said total VIZZ prescriptions rose more than 45% month over month in July, after telehealth (live 2026-07-06, $35 visit) and national TV launched, with all channels up. Q2 packs grew only ~9% q/q (~27,000). If August-September held even part of the July step-up, Q3 packs would be ~33-38k, product revenue ~$2.1-2.5M, and sequential growth 25-45%, a visible acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold its prints: 6 of the last 8 reactions were negative. The Q2 print carried the +45% July data and still fell 3.3%, then the stock fell another ~40% through September-October.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August, yet the stock has fallen from ~$5 to $3.14 since. The market is pricing the July spike as non-recurring (management itself said one month is not a trend). Had it priced sustained acceleration, the stock would not sit at ~0.55x estimated cash. What is unpriced is whether August-September held, and no IQVIA/Symphony series exists: management called retail tracking poor and ~60% of volume goes through ePharmacy.
findings.independence: The Fierce Healthcare telehealth launch piece (https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/telehealth/lenz-therapeutics-rolls-out-telehealth-offering-presbyopia-drops-vizz) confirms the channel and the $35 fee via Leerink, but carries no volume data. No independent script series was found.

findings.finding: Capital-allocation decision due with the print, on a stock at about half its cash. On the Q2 call, management said it would use Q3 data to decide which initiatives to keep and how much to invest in the next launch phase, and that it needs 'even more discipline in how we allocate capital'. Cash was $220.0M at 2026-06-30, against six-month operating cash use of $72.3M. On ~$35M of Q3 burn, Sep-30 cash would be ~$185M (~$5.9/share) against a ~$99M market cap at $3.14, so a cut in DTC or sales spend has a large asymmetric payoff. Continued full spend would confirm the burn the price already discounts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior spending-reset print at this company. 2026 prints that carried higher spend and weak launch metrics fell 17.9% and 20.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: An EV of roughly -$85M means the market is valuing the remaining cash as if most of it will be spent on the launch. If it expected a cost reset, the stock would trade nearer cash. The decision has not been announced: no 8-K since July, no WARN or layoff reports found, and the 10-Q still says SG&A 'will continue to increase in 2026'. The direction is inference, so the range is wide.
findings.independence: The cash and burn figures come from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001815776/000181577626000052/lenz-20260630.htm), a different document from the call quote. The 10-Q's language ('SG&A will continue to increase in 2026') cuts the other way, so this finding is sized net of it.

findings.finding: Crowded short covering into the print. FINRA short interest is 9.10M shares at 2026-10-15 (~29% of 31.42M shares outstanding; 31.6% of float per MarketBeat), with 11.8 days to cover on ~770-890k average volume. Short interest fell 13.9% from 10.56M on 2026-09-30 and 23% from 11.86M in mid-July. The stock sits at its 52-week low, ~0.55x estimated cash, with no ATM capacity left: the TD Cowen $150M ATM was fully used by 2025-12-31.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was ~21% of float in 2025 and 29-36% in 2026, and the stock still fell on most prints. The squeeze mechanism has not paid here so far; covering has accompanied the decline.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the information set more than a hidden fact. What matters is that 11.8 days to cover against a below-cash price means any non-negative print forces covering, while a bad print has little fresh supply left: FMR already halved to 5.7% by Aug 31 and the ATM is exhausted.
findings.independence: MarketBeat short-interest page (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LENZ/short-interest/): 31.57% of float, 11.81 days to cover, down 13.87%. Same FINRA data underneath, so not independent.

findings.finding: Competition through Q3. Tenpoint's Yuvezzi (carbachol/brimonidine) became available nationwide on 2026-03-30 and launched its first national DTC campaign on 2026-06-29, the same quarter as LENZ's national TV push. LENZ's own 10-Q added Yuvezzi, generic Vuity and Qlosi to its competition risk factor. Shared consumer attention could have damped VIZZ's August-September growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has been attributed to a competitor.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy: no Yuvezzi sales data exists and Tenpoint is private. The launch is public, so it is mostly priced; it is filed small for completeness.
findings.independence: Yuvezzi availability release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260330960621/en/YUVEZZI-from-Tenpoint-Therapeutics-Ltd.-Is-Now-Available-Nationwide-Across-the-United-States), a different document.

outside_window.finding: Greater China approval of aceclidine (Everest Medicines, which took over Corxel's rights on 2026-06-07) is expected in Q1 2027. LENZ is eligible for up to $85M in remaining regulatory and sales milestones.
EU MAA (validated March 2026) and UK MAA (April 2026) are under review. No CHMP opinion is plausible before 2027.

baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. The -18% 20-day run-up and the reaction history (6 of 8 prints down) argue for a negative reaction, while the findings net slightly positive on a cash floor and short covering. That cuts against the run-up, so p_up is held at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar has one source, MarketBeat only): the license-revenue/headline-miss finding was capped from -1.0 to -0.6.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold 6 of 8 prints): the July script momentum finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the strategy-decision finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because the 10-Q says SG&A will keep rising in 2026.
Lesson 5 (positioning is the information set, not a hidden fact): the short-interest finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8, though it stays filed under the core's rule to file every sourced fact.
Lesson 7 (look up short interest before negatives) was already done; it kept the negatives small. The competition proxy stands at -0.3 and p_up stays at 50.
